angle: WR/TE break mechanics from Combine route drills (Break G), graded with the same code on NFL snaps of the same route families (slant, out, hitch, in, corner), tested against full-season separation over expected (SOE) on held-out draft classes; last season's SOE as a day-3 tiebreaker with an explicit pick-gap rule and cost of being wrong; 2026 GO/HOLD calls with man/zone and slot/wide splits.
metric_name: Break G: mean acceleration (g) over the 1.0 s centred on the sharpest point of the first route break, z-scored within drill and Combine year and averaged over route drills; 1 sd = 0.021 g.
headline_number: -1.2 in of season SOE per sd of Break G [90%: -3.6, +1.0], n=116 receivers in unseen classes; a +3 in benefit is ruled out (bootstrap p 0.003), equivalence at +/-3 is not shown (TOST p 0.11). Baseline (pick, 40, weight, NGS, TE) held-out R2 0.00, Break G dR2 0.013 [-0.157, 0.085]. Drill-to-same-NFL-route correlation 0.02 [-0.27, 0.32]; 40 vs NFL top speed 0.43. Day-3 SOE gain 0.31 [-0.08, 0.63], receiver-clustered p 0.12 (bootstrap and shuffle agree), effective n about 19 of 20 pairs from 16 receivers.
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_17/revised applying all three judges' top_changes. Data science: one pre-specified day-3 test with a receiver-clustered shuffle that keeps the fitted season-fold models (p 0.12, matching the clustered bootstrap's 0.12) and an explanation of why the old all-pairs shuffle gave 0.01 (it also erased the training signal); design effect and effective n; Break G framed as a one-sided benefit test (p 0.003) plus TOST at +/-3 (p 0.11, not equivalent) and 89% of resamples inside the margin, removing the 'inside the margin' claim; verify.py (1.3 s) recomputes baseline R2, dR2, slope, the three speed rhos and the day-3 gains from data/processed + pairs_inputs.csv, speed_inputs.csv, baseline_inputs.csv and diffs against all_numbers.json (12/12 match); columns.json documents every CSV column. Football: decision-grade tiebreak rule from 106 same-season day-3 contrasts by pick-gap threshold (earlier pick 52% right, SOE 62%; a gap threshold under 32 picks adds +1 pt, so the rule is 'use SOE at any gap') with cost of being wrong (8.3 in / 1.2 catches vs 12.0 in / 1.8 catches for the pick) and expected saving per call; per-receiver SOE table split man/zone and slot/wide with cell n; 40-clip laser caveat; one speed definition (0.43) with 0.74 and 0.34 explained once; GO names lead, HOLD shrunk, flip condition per name at 150 routes, decision before March 2027 league year; 'earlier brief' sentences and leave-one-receiver-out history removed. Writeup: ~50-word lede in one unit; $1.08M and '60% signal' explained in plain terms; results directly after the decision table; analyst machinery moved to one appendix table. Viz: old Fig 4 split into Fig 4 (pairs, pick-gap curve, gains; clustered p in subtitle) and Fig 5 (2026 list with posterior intervals and split cells sized by n); Fig 2 shows both speed windows labelled.
open_risks: The day-3 tiebreaker is still unproven (p 0.12, every pick-gap interval includes zero); recommendation 3 is a lean and judges may want it demoted further.
The pick-gap threshold (32) was set before scoring but the 'use SOE at any gap' conclusion came after seeing the curve.
Per-receiver splits rest on 5-34 sampled snaps (half top-EPA); only 1 of 16 cells reaches 30 snaps, so the man/zone table is texture, not evidence.
Equivalence at +/-3 in fails (TOST p 0.11): the paper can only claim 'no benefit', not 'no effect'.
Word count is near the limit (~1,980) and Fig 4/Fig 5 are dense; the 2026 freeze (24 Oct 2026) is after the season began and the 2026 test has power 0.27.
